questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statement about aniline is false?
A. Aniline is a strong base than ammonia.
B. Aniline is a less basic than methylamine.
C. \(\mathrm{p} K_b\) of aniline is more than that of ammonia.
D. Aniline reacts with bromine water to form a white precipitate.
questions.solution: According to Lewis theory, the species which easily loses a pair of electron is Lewis base, lone pair on nitrogen in aniline are involved in resonance with the benzene ring and therefore not available for donation to that extent as in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\). Since, ammonia can lose easily electron pair while aniline cannot, thus ammonia is a stronger base than aniline.Thus, statement (A) is false. Hence, the correct option is (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: DNA consists of two polynucleotide chains, Each chain forms a right-handed spiral with how many bases in one turn of spiral?
questions.solution: Watson and Crick proposed that DNA molecule is in the form of a double helix with two polynucleotide chains coiled around one another in a spiral. This is known as B-DNA or biological DNA. It has 10 nucleotides pairs per turn of the double helix and is right handed with a diameter of \(20 Å\). One complete turn of the double helix is \(34 Å\). The distance between adjacent stacks or nucleotides is \(3.4 Å\). Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When glucose reacts with bromine water, the main product is

Hence, the correct option is (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements is correct about \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\) ?
A. The hybridisation of central atom is \(s p^3\).
B. Its resonance structure has one \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) single bond and two \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) double bonds.
C. The average formal charge on each carbon atom is 0.67 units.
D. All \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond lengths are equal.
questions.solution:
The hybridisation of central atom is \(s p^2\). Since a net charge of -2 is shared over 3 oxygen atoms, hence formal charge \(=0.67\) units. In resonating structures bonds are not fixed and therefore, all bond lengths are equal.
Hence, options (c) and (d) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of \(\mathrm{I}_3^{-}\)ion?
questions.solution:
\(\mathrm{I}_3^{-}\)molecular geometry is linear. While there are three iodine atoms, one of the atoms has a negative charge which further gives 3 lone pairs of electrons and 2 bond pairs.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The supply of oxygen to tissues by blood, can be explained by
questions.solution:
Le-Chatelier's principle drives the following reaction forward as blood passes through the alveoli
\(\mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{HCO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\)
The carbon dioxide produced here continually diffuses into the alveoli and is exhaled, ensuring favorable kinetics for the reaction to proceed. Thus, correct answer is option (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reversible reaction, if the concentration of reactants is increased, the equilibrium constant of the reaction
questions.solution: Equilibrium constant is independent of change in concentration of reactants or products. It depends only on temperature. Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Find the correct order of the given elements with respect to their size
questions.solution:
\(\mathrm{Zn}\) atomic radii is \(137 \mathrm{pm}\)
\(\mathrm{Fe}\) atomic radii is \(126 \mathrm{pm}\)
\(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) ionic radius is \(63 \mathrm{pm}\),
\(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) has an ionic radius of \(77 \mathrm{pm}\).
Thus, the correct order of their size is
\(\mathrm{Zn}  \gt  \mathrm{Fe}  \gt  \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}  \gt  \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\)
Hence, the correct option is (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The possible oxidation states of group 13 elements is/are
questions.solution: The general oxidation state exhibited by the group 13 elements in the group are +3 and +1 due to its general electronic configuration \(n s^2, n p^1\). As we go down the group of boron family, the tendency to form +1 ion increases. This is due to inert pair effect. Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which element of the \(3 d\)-series has highest third ionisation enthalpy?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of zinc metal is
\(\mathrm{Zn} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^{10}, 4 s^2\)
The third ionisation enthalpy of \(\mathrm{Zn}\) means removal of electron from the stable configuration of \(3 d^{10}\).
The metal having the highest third ionisation enthalpy is \(\mathrm{Zn}\). Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the cell \(\mathrm{Zn}\left|\mathrm{Zn}^{+2} \| \mathrm{Cu}^{+2}\right| \mathrm{Cu}\) ?
questions.solution:
In the Daniell cell, copper and zinc electrodes are immersed in a solution of copper(II) sulphate and zinc sulphate, respectively.
At the anode (negative electrode), zinc is oxidised per the following half reaction.
\(\mathrm{Zn}(s) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(a q)+2 e^{-}\)
At the cathode (positive electrode), copper is reduced per the following reaction.
\(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(a q)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}(s)\)
Overall cell reaction is
\(\mathrm{Zn}(s)+\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(a q) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(a q)+\mathrm{Cu}(s)\)
These processes result in the accumulation of solid copper at the cathode and the corrosion of the zinc electrode into the solution as zinc cations. Hence, the correct option is (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a compound with empirical formula \(\mathrm{C}_7 \mathrm{H}_8 \mathrm{O}\), how many aromatic structures are possible?
questions.solution:
For the compound having formula \(\mathrm{C}_7 \mathrm{H}_8 \mathrm{O}\) there are 5 aromatic isomers. (1) Benzyl alcohol (2) o-methyl phenol (3) \(m\)-methyl phenol (4) \(p\)-methyl phenol (5) Anisole
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following can show geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
There are two geometrical isomer of 1, 2-dichloroethene, one is called cis -1, 2-dichloroethene and the other is called trans-1, 2-di-chloroethene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The common name of isopropyl benzene is
questions.solution:
Cumene, also known as isopropyl benzene or 2-phenylpropane, belongs to the class of organic compounds known as cumenes.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct order of decreasing acid strength of following acids is
(1) trichloro acetic acid
(2) trifluoro acetic acid
(3) acetic acid
(4) formic acid
questions.solution:
As \(-I\)-effect increases, \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) group becomes more electron deficient and tendency to loose \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\)ions increases i.e., acid strength increases. As \(+I\) effect increases. Acid strength decreases. Thus, correct order of acid strength is : trichloroacetic acid  >  trifluoroacetic acid  >  forminc acid  >  acetic acid.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of increasing acidic strength among the following is
options: phenol < ethanol < chloroacetic acid < acetic acid
ethanol  < phenol < chloroacetic acid < acetic acid
ethanol  < phenol < acetic acid < chloroacetic acid
chloroacetic acid  < acetic acid < phenol \( \lt  \) ethanol
questions.solution:
The correct order of increasing acidic strength is : ethanol \( \lt  \) phenol \( \lt  \) acetic acid \( \lt  \) chloroacetic acid Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because in phenol, the phenoxide ion obtained on deprotonation is stabilised by resonance, which is not possible in case on ethanol.
Also carboxylic acids are more acidic than alcohols and phenols as the carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance. Chloroacetic acid is more acidic than acetic acid due to inductive effect of chlorine atom which stabilises the carboxylate anion.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkenes will yield 2-methyl propanal on reductive ozonolysis. (addition with ozone followed by the reaction with \(\mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) ).
questions.solution:
2,5 dimethyl hex -3-ene on reductive ozonolysis in presence of \(\mathrm{O}_3\) and \(\mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\), gives 2 moles of 2-methyl propanal.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements of which of the following group(s) of periodic table do not form hybrides?
questions.solution: The region of the periodic table from group 7 to 9 is referred to as the hydride gap as they do not form hydrides. Examples of such elements are \(\mathrm{Mn}, \mathrm{Fe}, \mathrm{Co}, \mathrm{Ru}\) etc. These elements do not form hydrides on account of low affinity for hydrogen in their normal oxidation states. Hence, the correct option is (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molar ratio of a weak acid \(\mathrm{H} A\left(K_a=10^{-6}\right)\) and its salt with strong base, so that the \(\mathrm{pH}\) of buffer solution is 6 .
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]} \log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{pH}}{\mathrm{p} K_a}=\frac{6}{6}=1 \\
& {\left[K_a=10^{-6} \therefore \mathrm{p} K_a=-\log K_a=\log \left(10^{-6}\right) \Rightarrow 6\right]} \\
& \log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]}=1 \\
& \frac{[\text { Acid }]}{[\text { Salt }]}=10^{-1} \text { or } 0.1
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the correct option is (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following mineral acids can attack \(\mathrm{SiO}_2\) ?
questions.solution: Although hydrofluoric acid (HF) is a weak acid, it does attack silicates very effectively. For this reason, its primary laboratory use is to attack and dissolve silicate minerals. Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A pungent smelling gas \(A\) gives dense white fumes with conc. \(\mathrm{HCl}\). When \(A\) reacts with alkaline solution of a colourless reagent \(B\), a reddish-brown precipitate \(C\) is formed. The compounds \(A, B, C\) respectively are

Nessler's reagent is a solution containing \(\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{HgI}_4\) and \(\mathrm{KOH}\). lodide and mercury ions react with ammonia under alkaline conditions to produce a reddish brown complex, iodide of million's base \(\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{Hg}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Hg}-\mathrm{I}\right)\) formed.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

Find the product of the following reaction, when \(\mathrm{Xe}\) is taken in excess,

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metallic solid undergoes Frenkel defect. Its original mass, volume and density are \(M_0, V_0\) and \(D_0\) respectively. After Frenkel defect the mass, volume and density are \(M, V\) and \(D\) respectively. The variations of \(M, V\) and \(D\) after Frenkel defect are
questions.solution: In Frenkel defect, atoms remain within the solid crystal. Only one vacancy is created. Density remains the same. Thus, \(M=M_0, V=V_0\) and \(D=D_0\). Hence, the correct option is (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following materials is extensively used as a piezoelectric material ?
questions.solution: Piezoelectric materials are materials that have the ability to generate internal electrical charge from applied mechanical stress. Quartz and Rochelle salt demonstrated the highest piezoelectric effects. Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In comparison to a \(0.01 \mathrm{M}\) solution of glucose, the depression in freezing point of a \(0.01 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{MgCl}_2\) solution is (Molecular weight of \(\mathrm{MgCl}_2=95\), molecular weight of glucose \(=180\) ).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the concentration of fluorine in ppm in \(500 \mathrm{~g}\) of toothpaste containing \(0.2 \mathrm{~g}\) of fluorine.
questions.solution:
PPM or Parts Per Million is expressed as 1 milligram of substance per kilogram of parent substance.
Since, mass of toothpaste \(=500 \mathrm{~g}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg}\), and mass of fluoride ion \(=0.2 \mathrm{~g}=200 \mathrm{mg}, 0.5 \mathrm{~kg}\) toothpaste contains \(200 \mathrm{mg}\) fluoride ions, \(1 \mathrm{~kg}\) toothpaste will contain \(200 \times 2=400 \mathrm{mg}\) fluoride ions.
Hence, concentration of fluoride ion is \(400 \mathrm{ppm}\) or \(4 \times 10^2 \mathrm{ppm}\). Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A \(40 \%\) by mass sucrose solution is heated till, it becomes \(50 \%\) by mass. Calculate the mass of water lost from \(100 \mathrm{~g}\) of the solution is
questions.solution:
\(40 \%\) sucrose solution means it contains \(60 \%\) water. After heating, till \(50 \%\) by mass sucrose remains.
Thus, \(\%\) water lost \(=\frac{0.4}{0.5} \times 100=80\)
Water lost \(=100-80=20 \mathrm{~g}\)
Hence, statement (c) is correct.

When \(10 \mathrm{~g}\) of copper and \(10 \mathrm{~g}\) of iodine are mixed, calculate the theoretical yield of CuI according to the equation,

questions.q: At STP, if 5.6 litres of a gas weights \(7.5 \mathrm{~g}\), then identify the gas.
questions.solution:
One mole of gas at STP occupies \(22.4 \mathrm{~L}\).
Thus, 5.6 L of gas at STP contains 0.25 moles.
Number of moles \(=\) weight in gram \(/\) molecular weight
\(\begin{aligned}
0.25 & =7.5 / M \\
M & =30
\end{aligned}\)
Thus, the gas is NO.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the ratio of the effusion of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{N}_2\), when temperature and pressure gradients are held constant?
questions.solution:
The rate of effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of the mass of its particles.
Rate of effusion \(\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\text { Molecular mass }}}\)
If two gases \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{N}_2\) are at the same temperature and pressure, the ratio of their effusion rates is inversely proportional to the ratio of the square roots of their molar masses.
\(\frac{\text { Rate effusion of } \mathrm{CO}}{\text { Rate of effusion of } \mathrm{N}_2} \propto \frac{\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{N}_2}}}{\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{CO}}}}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{\frac{28}{28}} \Rightarrow 1: 1\)
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of a given mass of a gas is directly proportional to its Kelvin temperature at constant pressure. The above statement is known as ____
questions.solution:
The variation in a volume of a gas with temperature was first studies by Jacques Charles (1787) and known as Charles' law.
Charles' law states as, "The volume of the given mass of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant pressure. Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the temperature of 4 moles of a gas occupying \(5 \mathrm{~L}\) volume at 3.32 bar? \(\left(R=0.083\right.\) bar \(\mathrm{L} \mathrm{K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\) )
questions.solution:
Given, \(n=4\) moles,
\(\begin{gathered}
\text {volume }=5 \mathrm{~L}, \text { pressure }=3.32 \mathrm{bar}, \\
R=0.083 \text { bar } \mathrm{L} \mathrm{K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{gathered}\)
Calculate \((T)=\) ?
Apply ideal gas equation, \(p V=n R T\)
\(\Rightarrow T=\frac{p V}{n R}=\frac{3.32 \times 5}{4 \times 0.083} \Rightarrow 50 \mathrm{~K}\)
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate energy of half mole of photons of a radiation with frequency \(3 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{~Hz}\).
questions.solution:
Energy of a photon, \(E=h v\), where, \(v=\) frequency \(=3 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{~Hz}\)
Therefore, energy
\(=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{~Hz}=1.9878 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{~J}\)
1 mole \(=6.02 \times 10^{23}\) photons,
therefore, \(\frac{1}{2}\) mole \(=3.01 \times 10^{23}\) photons
Therefore, energy of \(\frac{1}{2}\) mole of photons
\(\begin{aligned}
& =1.9878 \times 10^{-21} \times 3.01 \times 10^{23} \\
& =0.5982 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the correct option is (b).

questions.q: Calculate the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in \({ }_{16}^{32} \mathrm{~S}^{2-}\).

An element can be represented as \({ }_Z^A X\). where, \(X=\) symbol of element
\(Z=\) atomic number or number of protons

Therefore, for \({ }_{16}^{32} \mathrm{~S}^{-2}\), number of protons \(=16\), number of neturons \(=32-16=16\) and electrons \(=18\)
Hence, the correct option is (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A charcoal cube having side length \(10 \mathrm{~cm}\) is chopped lengthwise into 5 equal pieces. Then the effective adsorption power
questions.solution:
Initial volume of cube \(=(10)^3=1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3\)
\(V\) when cube is chopped along length then it will form cuboid in which length \(=6 \mathrm{~cm}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\text {breadth } & =10 \mathrm{~cm} \\
\text {height } & =10 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)
Adsorption power \(\propto\) more surface area \(\propto 6 \mathrm{~cm}\)
\(\propto 6 \times(10)^2 \propto 600 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
Final surface area of the cuboid
\(\begin{aligned}
& =2(l \times b+b \times h+h \times l) \text { Area of cuboid } \\
& =2(2 \times 10+100+20) \\
& =280 \mathrm{~cm}^2
\end{aligned}\)
For final cuboid area \(=280 \times 5=1400 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
So, final adsorption power \(\propto 1400 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\frac{\text { Final adsorption power }}{\text { Initial adsorption power }} & =\frac{1400}{600}=\frac{14}{6}=\frac{7}{3} \\
& =2.33 \text { times }
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction, \(2 \mathrm{NH}_3(s)+\mathrm{CO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_2 \mathrm{CONH}_2(a q)+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(t)\), find the value of equilibrium constant at 295 K. Given, standard Gibbs energy change at the given temperature is \(13.9 \mathrm{kJmol}^{-1}\).
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Delta G^{\circ}=-2.303 n R T \log K_C \\
& -13.9 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J}=-2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 295 \log K_C \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log K_C=\frac{-13.9 \times 10^3}{-2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 295}=2.46 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad K_C=10^{2.46} \Rightarrow 288.4=2.88 \times 10^2
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following processes, for which process, the change in entropy \((\Delta S)\) is negative?
questions.solution: When water freezes its entropy decreases. A negative change in entropy indicates that the disorder of an isolated system has decreased. When liquid water freezes into ice represents an isolated decrease in entropy because liquid particles are more disordered than solid particles. Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the value of ' \(p\) ' and ' \(q\) ' if the function \(f(t)=t^3-6 t^2+p t+q\) defined on \([1,3]\) satisfies the Rolle's theorem for \(c=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}}\)

\(\begin{gathered}
f(1)=f(3) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 1-6+p+q=27-54+3 p+q \\
\Rightarrow \quad 2 p=22 \Rightarrow p=11 \text { and } q \in \mathbf{R} .
\end{gathered}\)
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the tangent to the curve \(x^{2 / 3}+y^{2 / 3}=a^{2 / 3}\) meets the \(X\)-axis at \(A\) and \(Y\)-axis at \(B\), then \(A B=\)
questions.solution:
Given curve is \(x^{2 / 3}+y^{2 / 3}=a^{2 / 3}\) ...(i)
Now, let a point on curve \(P\left(a \cos ^3 \theta, a \sin ^3 \theta\right)\)
On differentiating the curve (i) w.r.t \(x\), we get
\(\frac{2}{3} x^{-1 / 3}+\frac{2}{3} y^{-1 / 3} \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=-\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{1 / 3}\)
\(\therefore\) Slope of tangent at point \(P\) is
\(m=\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_P=-\tan \theta\)
\(\therefore\) Equation of the tangent of the curve at point \(P\) is
\(y-a \sin ^3 \theta=-\tan \theta\left(x-a \cos ^3 \theta\right) \quad ...(ii)\)
\(\because\) The tangent (ii) meets the axes at \(A\) and \(B\), so \(A(a \cos \theta, 0)\) and \(B(0, a \sin \theta)\)
\(\therefore \quad A B=\sqrt{a^2 \cos ^2 \theta+a^2 \sin ^2 \theta}=a\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The population of a city grows at the annual rate of \(3 \%\). What percentage increase is expected in \(5 \mathrm{yr}\) ?
questions.solution:
Let the population in begining is \(P_0\), then according to the question percentage increase in 5 yr expected is
\(\begin{aligned}
\frac{P_0\left(1+\frac{3}{100}\right)^5-P_0}{P_0} \times 100 & =\left[\left(\frac{103}{100}\right)^5-1\right] \times 100 \\
& =\left[(1.03)^5-1\right] \times 100 \\
& =[1.159-1] \times 100=15.9 \%
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The curve \(y=a x^3+b x^2+c x+5\) touches the \(X\)-axis at \(P(-2,0)\) and cuts \(Y\)-axis at a point \(Q\), where gradient is 3 . Then the values of \(a, b, c\) are
questions.solution:
The equation of given curve is
\(y=a x^3+b x^2+c x+5\) ...(i)
\(\because\) Curve (i) passes through point \(P(-2,0)\), so
\(-8 a+4 b-2 c+5=0\) ...(ii)
and curve (i) cuts the \(Y\)-axis at a point \(Q\) with gradient 3, so \(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_Q=3\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad 3 a x^2+2 b x+\left.c\right|_{x=0} \Rightarrow c=3\) ...(iii)
\(\because\) Point \(Q\) have coordinates \((0,5)\), so curve (i) passes through \(Q(0,5)\).
From Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we have \(8 a-4 b+1=0\). Now, from the options
\(c=3, a=-\frac{1}{2} \text { and } b=-\frac{3}{4}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If a Polynomial $x^4+x^2+1$ is divisible by $x^2+m x+1$ and $x^2+n x+1$. Then $m+n$ is equal to
(1) 2
(2) 0
(3) 3

On differentiating both sides w.r.t. \(x\), we get
\(n(1+x)^{n-1}=1 \cdot C_1+2 C_2 x+3 C_3 x^2+\ldots \ldots .+n C_n x^{n-1}\)

\(\begin{aligned}
& n\left[(1+x)^{n-1}+(n-1) x(1+x)^{n-2}\right] \\
& \quad=1^2 C_1+2^2 C_2 x+3^2 C_3 x^2+\ldots \ldots+n^2 C_n x^{n-1}

Put \(x=1\), we get

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If \(\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & -1 & x \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ x & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\) has no inverse, then the real value of \(x\) is
questions.solution:
It is given that matrix \(A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & -1 & x \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ x & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\) have no inverse, so
\(\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& |A|=0 \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & -1 & x \\
1 & x & 1 \\
x & -1 & 1
\end{array}\right| & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 1(x+1)+1(1-x)+x\left(-1-x^2\right) & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x+1+1-x-x-x^3 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow x^3+x-2=0 \Rightarrow(x-1)\left(x^2+x+2\right) & =0
\end{array}\)
Either \(x=1\) or \(x^2+x+2=0\)

\(\therefore|A|=0 \Rightarrow x=1\)
Hence, option (d) is correct

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the pairs of straight lines \(x^2-2 q x y-y^2=0\) and \(x^2-2 p x y-y^2=0\) bisect the angles between each other, then which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
It is given that the pair of straight lines \(x^2-2 p x y-y^2=0\) and \(x^2-2 q x y-y^2=0\) bisect, the angles between each other, then equations \(\frac{x^2-y^2}{1-(-1)}=\frac{x y}{-p}\) and \(x^2-2 q x y-y^2=0\) represents same line, so \(x^2+\frac{2}{p} x y-y^2=0\) represents \(x^2-2 q x y-y^2=0\) on comparing, we get \(\frac{2}{p}=-2 q\) \(\Rightarrow \quad p q+1=0\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If one of the lines \(2 x^2-x y+b y^2=0\) passes through the point \((-4,-2)\), then \(b^2=\)
questions.solution:

\(2 x^2-x y+b y^2=0\)

& 2(-4)^2-(-4)(-2)+b(-2)^2 =0 \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The point of intersection of the pair of lines \(x^2+x y+2 y^2-3 x+2 y+4=0\) is
questions.solution:
The point of intersection of the pair of lines \(f(x, y) \equiv x^2+x y+2 y^2-3 x+2 y+4=0\) is same as the intersection of curve obtaining after partial differentiating of the curve w.r.t. \(x\) and \(y\) respectively.
\(\begin{aligned}
\because & \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} =2 x+y-3=0 \quad \ldots (i) \\
\text {and } & \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =x+4 y+2=0 \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{aligned}\)
By cross-multiplication method, we get
\(\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& & \frac{x}{2+12} & =\frac{-y}{4+3}=\frac{1}{8-1} \\
\Rightarrow & (x, y) & =(2,-1)
\end{array}\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If slope of one line of \(a x^2+4 x y+y^2=0\) is 3 times the other, then the value of ' \(a\) ' is
questions.solution:
Let the slope of lines are \(m\) and \(3 m\) respectively which are represented by \(a x^2+4 x y+y^2=0\)
\(\because\) Sum of slopes \(=m+3 m=-\frac{4}{1}=-4 \Rightarrow m=-1\) and product of the slopes \(=m(3 m)=\frac{a}{1} \Rightarrow m^2=\frac{a}{3}\)
\(\therefore \quad(-1)^2=\frac{a}{3} \Rightarrow a=3\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the parabola \(y^2=12 x\) at \((3,-6)\) is
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the parabola \(y^2=8 x\) inclined at \(30^{\circ}\) to the \(X\)-axis is
questions.solution:

So, the equation of required tangent is

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the number of rectangles formed on a chess board is 1296, then the total number of squares formed on the chess board is
questions.solution:
It is given that the number of rectangles formed in chess board (Let having size \(n \times n\)) is 1296
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad{ }^{n+1} C_2 \times{ }^{n+1} C_2=1296 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2=1296=(36)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{n(n+1)}{2}=36 \Rightarrow n(n+1)=72 \Rightarrow n=8 \\
\end{aligned}\)
So, number of squares of any sizes are
\(\begin{aligned}
& n^2+(n-1)^2+(n-2)^2+\ldots \ldots .+1^2 \\
& =1^2+2^2+3^2+\ldots \ldots+8^2 \\
& =\frac{8 \times 9 \times 17}{6}=4 \times 3 \times 17=12 \times 17=204
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A number lock has 3 rings and each ring has 8 digits. Total number of different ways in which 3 rings can be rotated is
questions.solution: Since, it is given that a lock has 3 rings and each ring has 8 digits, so each ring can be rotated in 8 ways, therefore total number of different ways in which 3 rings can be rotated is \(8 \times 8 \times 8=8^3\). Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: In how many ways a committee of a 6 members can be formed out of 10 members but always consisting of a specified member ?
questions.solution: As the committee consists a specified member out of 6 members, then we need to select only 5 members out of 9 remaining members and it can be done is \({ }^9 C_5\) ways. Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For any two events, \(A, B\) if \(P(A \cup B)=a P(A \cap B)+b P(A)+c P(B)\), then \(3 a+2 b+5 c=\) ?
questions.solution:
As we know for any two events \(A\) and \(B\)
\(P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A \cap B)\)
Now, on comparing with the given equation
\(P(A \cup B)=a P(A \cap B)+b P(A)+c P(B)\)
Then, we get \(a=-1, b=1, c=1\)
\(\therefore \quad 3 a+2 b+5 c=3(-1)+2+5=4\)
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In 3 trials of a binomial distribution, the probability of 2 successes is 9 times the probability of 3 successes. Then the probability of success in each trial is
questions.solution:
In a 3 trials of a binomial distribution, the probability of 2 successes \(=9 \times\) probability of 3 successes
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad{ }^3 C_2 p^2 q=9\left({ }^3 C_3 p^3\right) \quad\{\text {where } p+q=1\} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3 p^2 q=9 p^3 \Rightarrow q=3 p \\
& \therefore p=\frac{1}{4}=\text { probability of success in each trial. }
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
A random variable \(X\) has the probability distribution as given below. Let \(E=[X \mid X\) is prime number] and \(F=\{X \mid X \lt  4\}\), then \(P(E \cup F)=\)
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline X & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
\hline P(X) & K & 2 K & K^2 & 2 K^2 & 5 K^2 & K & K & 2 K \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Given probability distribution is
\(\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}
\hline \boldsymbol{X} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
\hline P(X) & K & 2 K & K^2 & 2 K^2 & 5 K^2 & K & K & 2 K \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\because & \Sigma P(X) & =1 \\
\Rightarrow & 8 K^2+7 K & =1 \\
\Rightarrow & 8 K^2+7 K-1 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & 8 K^2+8 K-K-1 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & 8 K(K+1)-1(K+1) & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & K=\frac{1}{8} \text { as } K &   \gt  0 .
\end{aligned}\)
\(\because\) The events (given) \(E=\{x \mid x\) is a prime}
\(=\{2,3,5,7\}\)
and \(F=\{X \mid X  \lt  4\}=\{1,2,3\}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad P(E \cup F)=P(E)+P(F)-P(E \cap F) \\
& =\left(2 K+K^2+5 K^2+K\right)+\left(K+2 K+K^2\right)-\left(2 K+K^2\right) \\
& =6 K^2+4 K=6 \frac{1}{64}+\frac{4}{8}=\frac{38}{64}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a \(\triangle A B C, a=1, b=\sqrt{3}\) and \(\angle C=\pi / 6\). Then the measure of the third side \(c=\)
questions.solution:
In a \(\triangle A B C\), it is given that, \(a=1, b=\sqrt{3}\) and \(\angle C=\frac{\pi}{6}\), then by cosine law, we have
\(\begin{aligned}
\cos \frac{\pi}{6} & =\frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2 a b} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1+3-c^2}{2 \sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow 3=4-c^2 \\
\Rightarrow c^2=1 \Rightarrow c & = \pm 1 \Rightarrow c=1 \quad \{\because c=\text { length of side}\}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(p x^2+q x+r=0, p \neq 0\). If \(p, q, r\) are in AP and \(\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}=4\), then the value of \(|\alpha-\beta|\) is
questions.solution:
Since, \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are roots of quadratic equation \(p x^2+q x+r=0, p \neq 0\) and \(p, q, r\) are in AP such that
\(\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}=4\) ...(i)
Let the \(p=q-d\) and \(r=q+d\), where \(d\) is the common difference of AP
\(\therefore\) Sum of the roots \(\alpha+\beta=\frac{-q}{q-d}\)
and product of the roots \(\alpha \beta=\frac{q+d}{q-d}\)
\(\because\) from Eq. (i), we have
\(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha \beta}=4 \Rightarrow \frac{-q}{q+d}=4 \Rightarrow 5 q+4 d=0\) ...(ii)
Now, \(|\alpha-\beta|=\sqrt{(\alpha+\beta)^2-4 \alpha \beta}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{\frac{q^2}{(q-d)^2}-4 \frac{q+d}{q-d}}=\sqrt{\frac{q^2-4\left(q^2-d^2\right)}{(q-d)^2}} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{4 d^2-3 q^2}{(q-d)^2}}=\sqrt{\frac{4\left(-\frac{5}{4} q\right)^2-3 q^2}{\left(q+\frac{5}{4} q\right)^2}} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{\frac{25}{4}-3}{\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^2}}=\frac{2}{9} \sqrt{13}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q: Solve \((8-t)^2 \lt  \left(t^2-3 t-10\right)\)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of the cubes of three consecutive natural numbers is divisible by
questions.solution:
Let the three consecutive natural numbers \((n-1), n, n+1\) where \(n \geq 2\)
\(\therefore\) Sum of cubes of the three consecutive natural numbers is
\((n-1)^3+n^3+(n+1)^3=3 n^3+6 n=3 n\left(n^2+2\right)\)
For each value of \(n \geq 2\), the expression \(3 n\left(n^2+2\right)\) is divisible by 9 . Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The average marks of boys in a class is 40 and that of girls is 45 . The average marks of both boys and girls combined is 42 . Then the percentage of boys in the class is
questions.solution:
Let the number of boys and girls in the class are \(m\) and \(n\) respectively, so according to given informations,
Total marks of boys \(=40 \mathrm{~m}\)
and total marks of girls \(=45 n\)
and total marks of boys and girls \(=42(m+n)\)
\(\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & 40 m+45 n=42(m+n) \\
\Rightarrow & 2 m=3 n \Rightarrow \frac{m}{3}=\frac{n}{2}=\lambda \quad \text{(let)} \\
\therefore & m=3 \lambda \text { and } n=2 \lambda
\end{array}\)
So, the percentage of boys in the class is
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{m}{m+n} \times 100 \\
& =\frac{3 \lambda}{3 \lambda+2 \lambda} \times 100=\frac{3}{5} \times 100=60 \% \\
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean deviation from the mean of the series \((a),(a+d),(a+2 d), \ldots \ldots \ldots . .,(a+2 n d)\) is
questions.solution:
The mean of given series \(a, a+d, a+2 d, \ldots \ldots, a+2 n d\) is
\(\frac{\frac{2 n+1}{2}[2 a+(2 n) d]}{2 n+1}=(a+n d)=m\) (let)
So, the mean deviation \(=\frac{1}{2 n+1} \sum_{i=1}^{2 n+1}\left|x_i-m\right|\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{2 n+1}[|n d|+|n d-d|+|n d-2 d|+\ldots .+|n d-2 n d|] \\
& =\frac{2 d}{2 n+1}[n+(n-1)+(n-2)+\ldots .+1]=\frac{n(n+1) d}{2 n+1}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (b) is correct

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the circle circumscribing the triangle formed by the straight lines \(x+y=6\). \(2 x+y=4\) and \(x+2 y=5\) is given by
questions.solution:
Equation of circle circumscribing the triangle formed by the straight lines, \(x+y=6,2 x+y=4\) and \(x+2 y=5\) is
\(\begin{aligned}
& (x+y-6)(2 x+y-4)+\lambda(2 x+y-4)(x+2 y-5) \\
& +\mu(x+2 y-5)(x+y-6)=0
\end{aligned}\)
\(\because\) For a circle the coefficients of terms \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) must be equal and non-zero and coefficient of \(x y\) must be zero.
\(\therefore\) Coefficient of \(x^2=\) coefficient of \(y^2\)
\(\Rightarrow 2+2 \lambda+\mu=1+2 \lambda+2 \mu \Rightarrow \mu=1\)
and coefficient of \(x y=0\)
\(\Rightarrow 1+2+4 \lambda+\lambda+\mu+2 \mu=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-6 / 5 \text {. }\)
So, equation of required circle is
\(\begin{array}{ll}
(x+y-6)(2 x+y-4)-\frac{6}{5}(2 x+y-4)(x+2 y-5)+(x+2 y-5)(x+y-6)=0 \\
\Rightarrow 5(x+y-6)(3 x+3 y-9)-6(2 x+y-4)(x+2 y-5)=0 \\
\Rightarrow 5(x+y-6)(x+y-3)-2(2 x+y-4)(x+2 y-5)=0
\end{array}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & 5\left(x^2+x y-3 x+x y+y^2-3 y-6 x-6 y+18\right) \\
& -2\left(2 x^2+4 x y-10 x+x y+2 y^2-5 y-4 x\right. \\
\Rightarrow & x^2+y^2-45 x-45 y+90+28 x+26 y-40=0 \\
\Rightarrow & x^2+y^2-17 x-19 y+50=0
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In quadrilateral \(A B C D, \mathbf{A B}=\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{B C}=\mathbf{b}\), \(\mathbf{A D}=\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}\) if \(M\) is the midpoint of \(B C\) and \(N\) is a point on \(D M\) such that \(D N=\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) D M\), then \(5 \mathbf{A N}=\)
questions.solution:
It is given that for a quadrilateral \(A B C D\),
\(\mathbf{A B}=\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{B C}=\mathbf{b}, \mathbf{A D}=\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}\)
\(\therefore\) According to the question, \(\mathbf{B M}=\frac{\mathbf{b}}{2}\) and
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{D N}{N M}=\frac{4}{1} \quad\left\{\because D N=\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) D M \text { given }\right\} \\
& \therefore \quad \mathbf{A N}-\mathbf{A D}=\frac{4}{1}(\mathbf{A M}-\mathbf{A N}) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 5 \mathrm{AN}=4 \mathbf{A M}+\mathbf{A D}=4\left(\mathbf{a}+\frac{\mathbf{b}}{2}\right)+(\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}) \\
& =4 \mathbf{a}+2 \mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}=3(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})=3 \mathbf{A C} \\
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the length of the intercept made on the line \(y=a x\) by the lines \(y=2\) and \(y=6\) is less than 5
questions.solution:

(given)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In \(\triangle A B C\), the circle that touches the sides \(B C\) internally and other two sides \(A B\) and \(A C\) externally, is called
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If \(3 a+5 b+6 c=0\) then the family of lines \(a x+b y+c=0\) pass through the fixed point
questions.solution:
Given equation of family of lines
\(\begin{aligned}
& a x+b y+c=0 \\
& \because \quad 3 a+5 b+6 c=0, \text { so } a x+b y-\frac{3 a+5 b}{6}=0 \\

\end{aligned}\)
So, the family of lines passes through the fixed point \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\).
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The image of the point with position vector \((\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})\), in the plane \(\mathbf{r} \cdot(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})+3=0\) is
questions.solution:
Let the image of the point with position vector \((\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})\) in the plane \(\mathbf{r} \cdot(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})+3=0\) is \(\left(x_2, y_2, z_2\right)\), so
\(\frac{x_2-1}{2}=\frac{y_2-3}{-1}=\frac{z_2-4}{1}=-2 \frac{2-3+4+3}{4+1+1}=-2\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad x_2=-3, y_2=5 ; z_2=2\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the plane whose intercepts on \(x, y, z\) axes are \(1,2,4\) respectively is
questions.solution:

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let \(\mathbf{u}=-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}\) and \(\mathbf{v}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\). Then the component of \(\mathbf{v}\) on \(\mathbf{u}\) is

questions.solution:
Given trigonometric equation is

\(\Rightarrow 2 \tan x=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \tan x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{6}\) or \(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\)
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: When a moving body collides with a stationary body of \(n\) times its mass, then the amount of kinetic energy transferred to the stationary body is
questions.solution:
Suppose, mass of moving body is \(m_1\).
Mass of stationary body, \(M_2=n m_1\)
For elastic collision,
velocity of separation = velocity of approach
\(\begin{aligned}
v_2-v_1 & =u-0 \\
v_2-u & =v_1 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
By the law of conservation of momentum,
\(\begin{aligned}
m_1 u & =m_1 v_1+M_2 v_2 \\
\Rightarrow m_1 u & =m_1 v_1+n m_1 v_2 \\
u & =v_1+n v_2 \quad \ldots (ii) \\
u & =v_2-u+n v_2 \quad \text{[From Eq. (i)]} \\
\Rightarrow 2 u & =(n+1) v_2 \\
v_2 & =\frac{2 u}{n+1}
\end{aligned}\)
Putting this value in Eq. (i)
\(v_1=v_2-u=\frac{2 u}{n+1}-u=\frac{2 u-n u-u}{n+1}=\frac{(1-n) u}{n+1}\)
\(\therefore\) Kinetic energy of moving body of mass \(m_1\), before collision,
\(K_1=\frac{1}{2} m_1 u^2\)
Kinetic energy of stationary body after collision,
\(\begin{aligned}
K_2 & =\frac{1}{2} M_2 v_2^2=\frac{1}{2} n m_1\left(\frac{2 u}{n+1}\right)^2 \\
& =\frac{1}{2} m_1 u^2 \cdot \frac{4 n}{(n+1)^2}
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Amount of KE transferred to stationary body
\(=\frac{K_2}{K_1}=\frac{\frac{1}{2} m_1 u^2 \times \frac{4 n}{(n+1)^2}}{\frac{1}{2} m_1 u^2}=\frac{4 n}{(n+1)^2}\)

questions.solution:
Suppose, the mass of circular disc is \(M\). A square portion of diagonal \(r\) is cut from it. Assuming centre of mass of circle to be origin. Centre of mass of square portion will be at distance \(\frac{r}{2}\) from it.
\(\therefore\) Side of square \(=\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\)
Area of square \(=\left(\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2=\frac{r^2}{2}\)
Mass of square, \(m=M \times \frac{r^2 / 2}{\pi r^2}\)
\(m=\frac{M}{2 \pi}\)
Centre of a mass of remaining disc from the centre of disc,
\(\begin{aligned}
x & =M \times 0-\frac{m \times r / 2}{M-m}=\frac{-\frac{M}{2 \pi} \times \frac{r}{2}}{M-\frac{M}{2 \pi}}=\frac{-r}{4 \pi-2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{r}{2-4 \pi}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: The distance between the centre of moon and earth is \(D\) and mass of earth is 81 times the mass of moon. At what distance from the centre of the earth, the gravitational force will be zero?
questions.solution:
Let a unit mass \(m\) is present at a distance \(x\) from the earth, where gravitational force is zero.
\(\frac{G m M_e}{x^2}=\frac{G m M}{(D-x)^2}\)...(i)
where, \(M_e\) is mass of earth and \(M\) is mass of moon.
Given, \(M_e=81 \mathrm{M}\)
\(\therefore\) From Eq. (i), we have
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{G m 81 M}{x^2}=\frac{G m M}{(D-x)^2} \Rightarrow \frac{81}{x^2}=\frac{1}{(D-x)^2} \\
\Rightarrow & \left(\frac{9}{x}\right)^2=\frac{1}{(D-x)^2} \Rightarrow \frac{9}{x}=\frac{1}{D-x} \\
\Rightarrow & 9 D-9 x=x \Rightarrow 9 D=10 x \\
\Rightarrow & x= \frac{9 D}{10}
\end{aligned}\)

& A_1 v_1=A_2 v_2 \\

\Rightarrow & r_2^2=\frac{r_1^2 v_1}{v_2} \Rightarrow r_2^2=\frac{\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \times 1}{4} \\
\Rightarrow & r_2^2=10^{-4} \\
\Rightarrow & r_2=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow r_2=1 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}\)
\(\therefore\) Diameter of nozzle, \(d_2=2 r_2=2 \times 1=2 \mathrm{~cm}\)

questions.solution:
Terminal velocity of spherical ball falling through viscous liquid is given as

questions.q: What should be the diameter of a copper wire \(\left(Y=12 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\right)\) of length \(5 \mathrm{~m}\) to produce the same elongation produced by a \(5 \mathrm{~m}\) long aluminium wire \(\left(Y=7 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\right)\) of diameter \(3 \mathrm{~mm}\) with the same \(40 \mathrm{~kg}\) mass ?
questions.solution:
For copper wire, \(Y=12 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\)
Length, \(\quad l=5 \mathrm{~m}\),
\(F=m g=40 \times 10=400 \mathrm{~N}\)
We know that, \(Y=\frac{F l}{A \Delta l}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad \Delta l & =\frac{F l}{A Y}=\frac{400 \times 5}{\pi r^2 \times 12 \times 10^{10}} \\
\Delta l & =\frac{2000}{12 \pi r^2 \times 10^{10}} \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
For aluminium wire, \(Y=7 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\)
Diameter, \(d=3 \mathrm{~mm}=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}\)
\(\therefore \quad r=\frac{d}{2}=\frac{3 \times 10^{-3}}{2} \mathrm{~m}=1.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}\)
Similarly, \(\quad Y=\frac{F l}{A \Delta l}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \Delta l=\frac{F l}{A Y}=\frac{400 \times 5}{\pi\left(1.5 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2 \times 7 \times 10^{10}}\)
\(\Delta l=\frac{2000}{15.75 \pi \times 10^4}\) ...(ii)
According to given condition, \(\Delta l\) is same in both cases.
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\(\begin{array}{rlrl}
\therefore & \frac{2000}{12 \pi r^2 \times 10^{10}} & =\frac{2000}{15.75 \pi \times 10^4} \\
\Rightarrow & 12 r^2 & =15.75 \times 10^{-6} \\
r & = & 1.15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}=1.15 \mathrm{~mm}
\end{array}\)
\(\therefore\) Diameter, \(d=2 r=2 \times 1.15=2.3 \mathrm{~mm}\)

questions.q: A rocket is fired vertically from the ground with a resultant vertical acceleration of a \(10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\). Fuel is finished in \(1 \mathrm{~min}\) and it continues to move up. What is the maximum height reached ?
questions.solution:
Resultant vertical acceleration,
\(a=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\)
Height travelled by the rocket in \(1 \mathrm{~min}(60 \mathrm{~s})\),
\(\begin{aligned}
h & =u t+\frac{1}{2} a t^2 \\
& =0 \times 60+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times(60)^2 \\
& =18000 \mathrm{~m}=18 \mathrm{~km}
\end{aligned}\)
Velocity of rocket after \(1 \mathrm{~min}(60 \mathrm{~s})\),
\(v=u+a t=0+10 \times 60=600 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\)
After \(1 \mathrm{~min}\), when fuel of rocket is finished, then
\(u=600 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, a=-g=-9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\)
Hence, if rocket goes at height \(h_2\), then
\(\begin{aligned}
v^2-u^2 & =2 g h_2 \\
0-(600)^2 & =2(-9.8) h_2 \\
\Rightarrow \quad h_2 & =\frac{360000}{2 \times 9.8} \\
& =18367.3 \mathrm{~m}=18.4 \mathrm{~km}
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Maximum height travelled by rocket from ground \(=h_1+h_2=18+18.4=36.4 \mathrm{~km}\)

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive sample is \(T\). The fraction of the initial mass of the sample that decays in an interval \(T / 2\) is
questions.solution:
Fraction remains after \(n\) half-lives is given as
\(\frac{N}{N_0}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / T} \quad\) [where, \(T\) is half-life]
\(\Rightarrow \quad \frac{N}{N_0}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{T}}\)
Given, \(\quad t=\frac{T}{2}\)
\(\therefore \quad \frac{N}{N_0}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{T / 2}{T}}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)

questions.q: A rectangular metal plate \(8 \mathrm{~cm} \times 4 \mathrm{~cm}\) at \(127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) emits \(E \mathrm{Js}^{-1}\). If both length and breadth are halved and the temperature is raised to \(327^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\), the rate of emission is
questions.solution:
According to Stefan-Boltzmann's law, rate of emission of radiation from metal surface is given as,
\(\begin{aligned}
E & =\sigma A T^4 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{E_2}{E_1} & =\left(\frac{A_2}{A_1}\right)\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^4 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\text{Given, } A_1 & =8 \mathrm{~cm} \times 4 \mathrm{~cm} \\
& =3.2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2 \\
T_1 & =127+273=400 \mathrm{~K} \\
A_2 & =\frac{8}{2} \mathrm{~cm} \times \frac{4}{2} \mathrm{~cm} \\
& =4 \times 2 \mathrm{~cm}^2=8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2 \\
T_2 & =327+273=600 \mathrm{~K}
\end{aligned}\)
Putting these values in Eq. (i), we have
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{E_2}{E_1}=\left(\frac{8 \times 10^{-4}}{3.2 \times 10^{-3}}\right)\left(\frac{600}{400}\right)^4 \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{81}{16} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{E_2}{E_1}=\frac{81}{64} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad E_2=\frac{81}{64} E_1=\left(\frac{81}{64}\right) E \mathrm{Js}^{-1}\left[\because E_1=E \mathrm{Js}^{-1}\right] \\
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of a Carnot's engine is \(100 \%\) only when
options: ideal gas is used as a working substance
temperature of the sink is equal to absolute zero
source temperature is equal to the temperature of the sink
source temperature is equal to absolute zero
questions.solution:
The efficiency of Carnot's engine is given as
\(\eta=1-\frac{T_2}{T_1}\) ...(i)
where, \(T_1=\) temperature of source
and \(T_2=\) temperature of sink.
For \(100 \%\) efficiency, \(\eta=1\)
\(\therefore\) From Eq. (i), we get
\(1=1-\frac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow \frac{T_2}{T_1}=0 \Rightarrow T_2=0\)
Hence, temperature of \(\operatorname{sink} T_2\) is equal to absolute zero.

questions.q: The condition \(d Q=d W\) holds good in which of the following ?
questions.solution:
According to first law of thermodynamics,
\(d Q=d W+d U\) ...(i)
For isothermal process, there is no change in internal energy.
Hence, \(d U=0\)
\(\therefore\) From Eq. (i), we get
\(d Q=d W\)
Hence, above equation holds good for isothermal process.

questions.q: \(306 \mathrm{~J}\) of heat is required to raise the temperature of 2 moles of an ideal gas at constant pressure from \(25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) to \(35^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\). The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of the same gas through the same range at constant volume is
questions.solution:
Given, at constant pressure heat
\(Q_p=306 \mathrm{~J}\)
Number of mole, \(n=2\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\Delta T & =T_2-T_1 \\
& =35-25=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}\)
We know that,
\(Q_p=n C_p \Delta T\)
\(\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & 306=2 C_p \times 10 \\
\Rightarrow & C_p=\frac{306}{2 \times 10} \\
\Rightarrow & C_p=15.3 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{K}
\end{array}\)
According to Mayer's formula,
\(\begin{aligned}
& C_p-C_V =R \\
\Rightarrow & C_V =C_p-R=15.3-8.314 \\
\Rightarrow & C_V =6.986 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{K}
\end{aligned}\)
The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of gas at constant volume through same range of temperature.
\(\begin{aligned}
Q_V & =n C_V \Delta T \\
& =2 \times 6.986 \times(35-25) \\
& =2 \times 6.986 \times 10 \\
& =139.72 \simeq 140 \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}\)
